blocks.content: The Chairperson and members of the Commission are appointed by the President on the recommendations of a six-member committee.

rows: Retired Chief Justice of India or retired Supreme Court Judge
Serving/retired SC Judge or serving/retired High Court Chief Justice
Persons having knowledge/practical experience in Human Rights (min. 1 woman)
Chairpersons of National Commissions (NCSC, NCST, NCW, NCM, NCBC, NCPCR, CCPD)

items: Selection Committee Composition: Prime Minister (Chair), Speaker of Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha, Leaders of Opposition in both Houses, and Union Home Minister.
Tenure: The Chairperson and members hold office for 3 years or until reaching 70 years of age, whichever is earlier, and are eligible for re-appointment.
7 Ex-Officio Members: Chairpersons of NCSC, NCST, NCW, NCM, NCBC, NCPCR, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) is a statutory body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
The Commission consists of a Chairperson, 5 full-time members, and 7 ex-officio members.
The Chairperson must be a retired Chief Justice of India or a retired Judge of the Supreme Court.
Out of the three human rights expert members, at least one must be a woman.
Members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a high-level 6-member committee headed by the Prime Minister.
